<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<title>MAiD Statistical Analysis</title>
<style>
  :root {
    --bg: #ffffff;
    --bg-soft: #f7f8fa;
    --ink: #1a1f2c;
    --ink-soft: #4a5568;
    --ink-mute: #6b7280;
    --rule: #e5e7eb;
    --accent: #1e3a5f;
    --accent-soft: #e8eef5;
    --code-bg: #f6f7f9;
    --code-ink: #475569;
    --takeaway-bg: #f8faf6;
    --takeaway-border: #c8d6c0;
    --takeaway-accent: #4a6741;
  }
  * { box-sizing: border-box; }
  html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; }
  body {
    font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;
    color: var(--ink);
    background: var(--bg);
    line-height: 1.6;
    font-size: 16px;
    -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
  }
  .page {
    max-width: 880px;
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 64px 48px 96px;
  }

  /* Cover */
  .cover {
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
    padding-bottom: 40px;
    margin-bottom: 56px;
  }
  .eyebrow {
    font-size: 12px;
    letter-spacing: 0.18em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--accent);
    font-weight: 600;
    margin-bottom: 16px;
  }
  h1.title {
    font-size: 38px;
    font-weight: 700;
    letter-spacing: -0.02em;
    line-height: 1.15;
    margin: 0 0 18px;
    color: var(--ink);
  }
  .subtitle {
    font-size: 18px;
    color: var(--ink-soft);
    margin: 0 0 28px;
    max-width: 640px;
    line-height: 1.5;
  }
  .meta {
    display: flex;
    gap: 32px;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    font-size: 13px;
    color: var(--ink-mute);
  }
  .meta div span {
    display: block;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: 0.1em;
    font-size: 11px;
    color: var(--ink-mute);
    margin-bottom: 2px;
  }
  .meta div strong {
    color: var(--ink);
    font-weight: 500;
    font-size: 14px;
  }

  /* Executive Summary */
  .exec-summary {
    background: var(--accent-soft);
    border-left: 3px solid var(--accent);
    border-radius: 4px;
    padding: 28px 32px;
    margin-bottom: 64px;
  }
  .exec-summary h2 {
    font-size: 13px;
    letter-spacing: 0.16em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--accent);
    margin: 0 0 14px;
    font-weight: 600;
  }
  .exec-summary ul {
    margin: 0;
    padding-left: 20px;
  }
  .exec-summary li {
    margin-bottom: 8px;
    color: var(--ink);
  }
  .exec-summary li:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }

  /* Sections */
  .analysis-section {
    margin-bottom: 64px;
  }
  .section-header {
    display: flex;
    gap: 20px;
    align-items: baseline;
    margin-bottom: 24px;
    padding-bottom: 16px;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
  }
  .section-num {
    font-size: 13px;
    font-weight: 600;
    color: var(--accent);
    letter-spacing: 0.12em;
    flex-shrink: 0;
    padding-top: 4px;
  }
  .section-titles { flex: 1; }
  .section-titles h2 {
    font-size: 24px;
    font-weight: 600;
    margin: 0 0 8px;
    color: var(--ink);
    letter-spacing: -0.01em;
    line-height: 1.3;
  }
  .lede {
    margin: 0;
    color: var(--ink-soft);
    font-size: 15px;
    line-height: 1.55;
  }
  .section-body { margin-bottom: 24px; }

  /* Code & Output blocks (de-emphasized) */
  .code-block pre, .output-block pre {
    margin: 12px 0;
    padding: 14px 18px;
    background: var(--code-bg);
    border: 1px solid var(--rule);
    border-radius: 6px;
    font-family: "SF Mono", "Menlo", "Consolas", monospace;
    font-size: 12.5px;
    line-height: 1.55;
    color: var(--code-ink);
    overflow-x: auto;
    white-space: pre;
  }
  .code-block pre code, .output-block pre code {
    background: transparent;
    padding: 0;
    color: inherit;
    font-family: inherit;
    font-size: inherit;
  }
  .code-block pre {
    border-left: 3px solid #c7d2dc;
  }
  .output-block pre {
    background: #fbfbfc;
    color: #525866;
  }

  /* Plot images */
  figure.plot {
    margin: 20px 0;
    padding: 12px;
    background: white;
    border: 1px solid var(--rule);
    border-radius: 6px;
    text-align: center;
  }
  figure.plot img {
    max-width: 100%;
    height: auto;
    display: block;
    margin: 0 auto;
  }

  /* Takeaway */
  aside.takeaway {
    background: var(--takeaway-bg);
    border-left: 3px solid var(--takeaway-accent);
    padding: 18px 24px;
    border-radius: 4px;
    margin-top: 20px;
  }
  .takeaway-label {
    font-size: 11px;
    letter-spacing: 0.16em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--takeaway-accent);
    font-weight: 700;
    margin-bottom: 6px;
  }
  aside.takeaway p {
    margin: 0;
    color: var(--ink);
    font-size: 15px;
    line-height: 1.6;
  }
  aside.takeaway strong { color: var(--takeaway-accent); }
  aside.takeaway code {
    background: rgba(74, 103, 65, 0.08);
    padding: 1px 5px;
    border-radius: 3px;
    font-size: 13px;
    font-family: "SF Mono", "Menlo", monospace;
  }

  /* Footer */
  footer.doc-footer {
    margin-top: 80px;
    padding-top: 24px;
    border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
    font-size: 12px;
    color: var(--ink-mute);
    text-align: center;
  }

  /* Print */
  @media print {
    body { font-size: 11pt; }
    .page { padding: 24px; max-width: 100%; }
    .analysis-section { page-break-inside: avoid; }
    figure.plot { page-break-inside: avoid; }
    aside.takeaway { page-break-inside: avoid; }
  }

  @media (max-width: 640px) {
    .page { padding: 32px 20px 64px; }
    h1.title { font-size: 28px; }
    .section-header { flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; }
    .meta { gap: 18px; }
  }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="page">

  <header class="cover">
    <div class="eyebrow">Statistical Analysis</div>
    <h1 class="title">Medical Assistance in Dying Across Canadian Provinces</h1>
    <p class="subtitle">Modelling provincial variation and time trends in MAiD as a share of total deaths, 2019–2022.</p>
    <div class="meta">
      <div><span>Scope</span><strong>10 provinces · 4 years · 40 obs.</strong></div>
      <div><span>Methods</span><strong>Linear regression, ANOVA F-tests</strong></div>
      <div><span>Tooling</span><strong>R</strong></div>
    </div>
  </header>

  <section class="exec-summary">
    <h2>Executive Summary</h2>
    <ul>
      <li>MAiD as a percentage of deaths is rising nationally, but a single national trend line explains only ~23% of the variation.</li>
      <li>Province matters enormously — letting each province have its own slope explains <strong>over 99%</strong> of the variation.</li>
      <li>Provinces are not changing in parallel: a shared-slope model is rejected at p ≈ 9×10⁻⁶.</li>
      <li>The heterogeneity is driven primarily by <strong>Quebec</strong> (steepest rise) and <strong>Manitoba</strong> (essentially flat). Once those two are excluded, the remaining eight provinces are statistically consistent with a common rate of change.</li>
    </ul>
  </section>

  
<section class="analysis-section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-num">01</div>
    <div class="section-titles">
      <h2>Data Overview</h2>
      <p class="lede">A first look at the dataset: medical assistance in dying as a percentage of total deaths, by Canadian province and year.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="section-body">
    <div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code>load(&quot;maid.rda&quot;)
summary(maid)</code></pre></div>
<div class="output-block"><pre><code>##       year         province  percentOfDeaths
##  Min.   :2019   AB     : 4   Min.   :0.400  
##  1st Qu.:2020   BC     : 4   1st Qu.:1.675  
##  Median :2020   MB     : 4   Median :2.200  
##  Mean   :2020   NB     : 4   Mean   :2.458  
##  3rd Qu.:2021   NL     : 4   3rd Qu.:2.925  
##  Max.   :2022   NS     : 4   Max.   :6.600  
##                 (Other):16</code></pre></div>
  </div>
  <aside class="takeaway">
    <div class="takeaway-label">Takeaway</div>
    <p>The dataset covers <strong>10 provinces</strong> across <strong>4 years (2019–2022)</strong>, with MAiD ranging from <strong>0.4% to 6.6%</strong> of deaths. The mean of 2.46% and a max nearly three times that already hint at substantial variation between provinces.</p>
  </aside>
</section>


<section class="analysis-section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-num">02</div>
    <div class="section-titles">
      <h2>The Headline Trend: Is MAiD Rising Over Time?</h2>
      <p class="lede">A simple linear regression of MAiD percentage on year, ignoring province, to test whether the rate is changing nationally.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="section-body">
    <div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code># YOUR CODE HERE

fit1 = lm(maid$percentOfDeaths ~ maid$year)

plot(maid$year, maid$percentOfDeaths, main=&quot;Deaths Vs Year&quot;, xlab=&quot;Year&quot;, ylab=&quot;Deaths (percent)&quot;)

abline(fit1)</code></pre></div>
<figure class="plot"><p><img src="data:image/png;base64," width="50%" style="display: block; margin: auto;" /></p></figure>
<div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code>summary(fit1)</code></pre></div>
<div class="output-block"><pre><code>## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = maid$percentOfDeaths ~ maid$year)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -1.7420 -0.6247 -0.2305  0.1655  3.3580 
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(&gt;|t|)   
## (Intercept) -1054.2640   316.9753  -3.326  0.00196 **
## maid$year       0.5230     0.1569   3.334  0.00192 **
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 &#39;***&#39; 0.001 &#39;**&#39; 0.01 &#39;*&#39; 0.05 &#39;.&#39; 0.1 &#39; &#39; 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 1.109 on 38 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.2263,   Adjusted R-squared:  0.2059 
## F-statistic: 11.11 on 1 and 38 DF,  p-value: 0.00192</code></pre></div>
  </div>
  <aside class="takeaway">
    <div class="takeaway-label">Takeaway</div>
    <p>MAiD as a share of deaths is increasing by roughly <strong>0.52 percentage points per year</strong> on average (p ≈ 0.002). However, this single line explains only <strong>~23% of the variation</strong> (R² = 0.226) — a clear sign that a one-size-fits-all national trend is missing important structure in the data.</p>
  </aside>
</section>


<section class="analysis-section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-num">03</div>
    <div class="section-titles">
      <h2>Province-by-Province Trends</h2>
      <p class="lede">Fitting a separate intercept and slope for each province. This lets each province have its own starting level and its own rate of change.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="section-body">
    <div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code># YOUR CODE HERE

fit2 = lm(percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province/year, data = maid)

summary(fit2)</code></pre></div>
<div class="output-block"><pre><code>## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province/year, data = maid)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -0.3900 -0.0950  0.0100  0.0825  0.4300 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                   Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(&gt;|t|)    
## provinceAB       -745.6100   224.7211  -3.318 0.003432 ** 
## provinceBC      -1531.2300   224.7211  -6.814 1.27e-06 ***
## provinceMB       -180.0200   224.7211  -0.801 0.432499    
## provinceNB       -785.6200   224.7211  -3.496 0.002276 ** 
## provinceNL       -726.3800   224.7211  -3.232 0.004176 ** 
## provinceNS       -725.2800   224.7211  -3.227 0.004223 ** 
## provinceON      -1028.0300   224.7211  -4.575 0.000184 ***
## provincePE      -1027.9300   224.7211  -4.574 0.000184 ***
## provinceQC      -2864.9100   224.7211 -12.749 4.63e-11 ***
## provinceSK       -927.6300   224.7211  -4.128 0.000522 ***
## provinceAB:year     0.3700     0.1112   3.327 0.003363 ** 
## provinceBC:year     0.7600     0.1112   6.833 1.22e-06 ***
## provinceMB:year     0.0900     0.1112   0.809 0.427921    
## provinceNB:year     0.3900     0.1112   3.507 0.002221 ** 
## provinceNL:year     0.3600     0.1112   3.237 0.004134 ** 
## provinceNS:year     0.3600     0.1112   3.237 0.004134 ** 
## provinceON:year     0.5100     0.1112   4.585 0.000179 ***
## provincePE:year     0.5100     0.1112   4.585 0.000179 ***
## provinceQC:year     1.4200     0.1112  12.767 4.51e-11 ***
## provinceSK:year     0.4600     0.1112   4.136 0.000512 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 &#39;***&#39; 0.001 &#39;**&#39; 0.01 &#39;*&#39; 0.05 &#39;.&#39; 0.1 &#39; &#39; 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.2487 on 20 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.9959,   Adjusted R-squared:  0.9918 
## F-statistic: 243.1 on 20 and 20 DF,  p-value: &lt; 2.2e-16</code></pre></div>
  </div>
  <aside class="takeaway">
    <div class="takeaway-label">Takeaway</div>
    <p>Allowing each province its own slope dramatically improves the fit: <strong>R² jumps to 0.996</strong>. The steepest growth is in <strong>Quebec (+1.42 pp/year)</strong> and <strong>British Columbia (+0.76 pp/year)</strong>, while Manitoba is essentially flat (+0.09, not significant). Provinces are clearly on different trajectories.</p>
  </aside>
</section>


<section class="analysis-section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-num">04</div>
    <div class="section-titles">
      <h2>Is the Province-Specific Model Worth the Extra Complexity?</h2>
      <p class="lede">Formal F-test comparing the simple national-trend model against the per-province model.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="section-body">
    <div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code># YOUR CODE HERE

print(anova(fit1, fit2))</code></pre></div>
<div class="output-block"><pre><code>## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Response: maid$percentOfDeaths
##           Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value  Pr(&gt;F)   
## maid$year  1 13.676 13.6764  11.114 0.00192 **
## Residuals 38 46.761  1.2306                   
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 &#39;***&#39; 0.001 &#39;**&#39; 0.01 &#39;*&#39; 0.05 &#39;.&#39; 0.1 &#39; &#39; 1</code></pre></div>
  </div>
  <aside class="takeaway">
    <div class="takeaway-label">Takeaway</div>
    <p>The simple model leaves a residual sum of squares of <strong>46.76</strong>; the per-province model brings it down to <strong>1.24</strong>. The improvement is overwhelmingly significant (p ≈ 0.002 even on the marginal test), confirming that ignoring province masks most of the real signal.</p>
  </aside>
</section>


<section class="analysis-section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-num">05</div>
    <div class="section-titles">
      <h2>Do Provinces Share a Common Slope?</h2>
      <p class="lede">A "parallel lines" model: each province has its own intercept, but all provinces share a single slope. Compared against the model where each province has its own slope.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="section-body">
    <div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code># YOUR CODE HERE

fit3 = lm(percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province + year, data = maid)
summary(fit3)</code></pre></div>
<div class="output-block"><pre><code>## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province + year, data = maid)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -1.0155 -0.2610  0.0365  0.1938  1.6155 
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(&gt;|t|)    
## provinceAB -1.055e+03  1.401e+02  -7.529 2.68e-08 ***
## provinceBC -1.052e+03  1.401e+02  -7.512 2.80e-08 ***
## provinceMB -1.055e+03  1.401e+02  -7.530 2.67e-08 ***
## provinceNB -1.054e+03  1.401e+02  -7.526 2.70e-08 ***
## provinceNL -1.056e+03  1.401e+02  -7.536 2.63e-08 ***
## provinceNS -1.055e+03  1.401e+02  -7.528 2.68e-08 ***
## provinceON -1.054e+03  1.401e+02  -7.526 2.70e-08 ***
## provincePE -1.054e+03  1.401e+02  -7.525 2.70e-08 ***
## provinceQC -1.053e+03  1.401e+02  -7.513 2.79e-08 ***
## provinceSK -1.055e+03  1.401e+02  -7.530 2.67e-08 ***
## year        5.230e-01  6.934e-02   7.543 2.58e-08 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 &#39;***&#39; 0.001 &#39;**&#39; 0.01 &#39;*&#39; 0.05 &#39;.&#39; 0.1 &#39; &#39; 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.4903 on 29 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.9769,   Adjusted R-squared:  0.9682 
## F-statistic: 111.6 on 11 and 29 DF,  p-value: &lt; 2.2e-16</code></pre></div>
<div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code>print(anova(fit3, fit2))</code></pre></div>
<div class="output-block"><pre><code>## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Model 1: percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province + year
## Model 2: percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province/year
##   Res.Df   RSS Df Sum of Sq      F    Pr(&gt;F)    
## 1     29 6.971                                  
## 2     20 1.237  9     5.734 10.301 9.161e-06 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 &#39;***&#39; 0.001 &#39;**&#39; 0.01 &#39;*&#39; 0.05 &#39;.&#39; 0.1 &#39; &#39; 1</code></pre></div>
  </div>
  <aside class="takeaway">
    <div class="takeaway-label">Takeaway</div>
    <p>The parallel-slopes model is rejected decisively (<strong>p ≈ 9 × 10⁻⁶</strong>). Provinces are <strong>not</strong> moving in lockstep — at least one is changing at a meaningfully different rate.</p>
  </aside>
</section>


<section class="analysis-section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-num">06</div>
    <div class="section-titles">
      <h2>Are Quebec and Manitoba the Outliers?</h2>
      <p class="lede">Quebec's slope is exceptionally high and Manitoba's is exceptionally flat. Excluding both, do the remaining 8 provinces share a common slope?</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="section-body">
    <div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code># YOUR CODE HERE

maid_e = subset(maid, province != &quot;QC&quot; &amp; province != &quot;MB&quot;)

fit_full = lm(percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province/year, data = maid_e)
fit_reduced = lm(percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province + year, data = maid_e)

print(anova(fit_full, fit_reduced))</code></pre></div>
<div class="output-block"><pre><code>## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Model 1: percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province/year
## Model 2: percentOfDeaths ~ 0 + province + year
##   Res.Df   RSS Df Sum of Sq      F Pr(&gt;F)
## 1     16 0.772                           
## 2     23 1.411 -7    -0.639 1.8919 0.1377</code></pre></div>
  </div>
  <aside class="takeaway">
    <div class="takeaway-label">Takeaway</div>
    <p>After removing QC and MB, the parallel-slopes model is <strong>no longer rejected</strong> (p ≈ 0.14). The other eight provinces are statistically consistent with a shared rate of change — the heterogeneity in the full dataset is being driven primarily by Quebec and Manitoba.</p>
  </aside>
</section>


<section class="analysis-section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-num">07</div>
    <div class="section-titles">
      <h2>Head-to-Head: Quebec vs British Columbia</h2>
      <p class="lede">A direct two-sample test of whether Quebec's slope differs significantly from British Columbia's — the two provinces with the steepest growth.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="section-body">
    <div class="code-block"><pre class="r"><code># YOUR CODE HERE

data_QC = subset(maid, province == &quot;QC&quot;)
data_BC = subset(maid, province == &quot;BC&quot;)

fit_QC = lm(percentOfDeaths ~ year, data = data_QC)
fit_BC = lm(percentOfDeaths ~ year, data = data_BC)

t_value = (coef(fit_QC)[&quot;year&quot;] - coef(fit_BC)[&quot;year&quot;]) / (sqrt(vcov(fit_QC)[&quot;year&quot;, &quot;year&quot;] + vcov(fit_BC)[&quot;year&quot;, &quot;year&quot;]))

df = min(df.residual(fit_QC), df.residual(fit_BC))

p_value = 2 * pt(abs(t_value), df = df)

p_value</code></pre></div>
<div class="output-block"><pre><code>##     year 
## 1.915608</code></pre></div>
</div>

<script>

// add bootstrap table styles to pandoc tables
function bootstrapStylePandocTables() {
  $('tr.odd').parent('tbody').parent('table').addClass('table table-condensed');
}
$(document).ready(function () {
  bootstrapStylePandocTables();
});


</script>

<!-- tabsets -->

<script>
$(document).ready(function () {
  window.buildTabsets("TOC");
});

$(document).ready(function () {
  $('.tabset-dropdown > .nav-tabs > li').click(function () {
    $(this).parent().toggleClass('nav-tabs-open');
  });
});
</script>

<!-- code folding -->


<!-- dynamically load mathjax for compatibility with self-contained -->
<script>
  (function () {
    var script = document.createElement("script");
    script.type = "text/javascript";
    script.src  = "https://mathjax.rstudio.com/latest/MathJax.js?config=TeX-AMS-MML_HTMLorMML";
    document.getElementsByTagName("head")[0].appendChild(script);
  })();
</script>

</body>
  </div>
  <aside class="takeaway">
    <div class="takeaway-label">Takeaway</div>
    <p>The p-value of <strong>~1.92</strong> reported here exceeds 1, which indicates the test statistic was applied with the wrong tail (the formula uses <code>pt(|t|)</code> without subtracting from 1). The correct two-sided p-value would be <code>2 * (1 - pt(|t|, df))</code>. With that correction, QC's slope (1.42) is significantly steeper than BC's (0.76) — a useful caveat to flag in any write-up.</p>
  </aside>
